name: Black Eyes
label: Dischord
lede: Two drummers face each other across the stage, a bassist stands at the front and another at the back, and one guitarist holds the middle. That was the whole band for three years and two albums, and they split before the second one came out. Twenty-one years after that, they made a third.

eras.title: Two kits, one middle
eras.text: The members came out of the house-show bands Trooper and the No-Gos. Dischord's bio lays out how they set up: a drummer on each side of the stage, a bassist at the back and one at the front, the guitarist in the middle. Shows turned into frenzied rhythmic jams that the crowd joined.

years.cap: Black Eyes live in a warehouse
years.h: Five people start playing as Black Eyes
years.p: In August 2001, [[Daniel Martin-McCormick|54e187d1-c4f3-4b5b-8eeb-e592a5573a29]], Hugh McElroy, Jacob Long, [[Dan Caldas|da0d355e-28bb-476b-8dbb-173e1899d097]] and [[Mike Kanin|a3234fdc-aa51-47af-986b-cc75c30f8a6d]] take the name. Most of them had already played together in Trooper and [[The No-Gos|15e434f9-fd72-4a37-9ced-0e65724f3302]].
years.xp:
Martin-McCormick played guitar, McElroy bass, Long bass and guitar, and Caldas and Kanin drums. McElroy and Martin-McCormick shared lead vocals.

With two full kits, the rhythm section could lock together or pull apart mid-song, and the band did both. Dischord's bio says the shows often dissolved into frenzied, rhythmic jams.

years.h: Some Boys, Shut Up, I Never: a 7" on McElroy's own label
years.p: Black Eyes' first record is a two-song 7" on Ruffian Records, the DIY label Hugh McElroy ran.

years.h: A split 7" with Early Humans on Planaria
years.p: Black Eyes contribute Have Been Murdered Again to a split with [[Early Humans|997f5443-1a25-44c5-af6e-aebf93b3fafc]] on Planaria Recordings.

eras.title: Gone before Cough
eras.text: Ian MacKaye produced the debut, and months on the road with Q and Not U followed. Then, with a second album finished and a saxophone added, Black Eyes broke up.

years.h: Black Eyes' self-titled debut, produced by MacKaye · Dischord No. 135
years.p: [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] produces and [[Don Zientara|a495882b-4585-4295-9269-e30c63f279fe]] records. Two vocalists and two full drum kits, with flashes of horn and synth over post-hardcore that wanted to dance.
years.xp: Dischord's bio places the band's debut in 2003, with tours alongside Q and Not U to follow. The zine later published for the 20th anniversary, Speaking In Tongues: Black Eyes 2001–2004, covers the band and the DC scene around it.

years.h: Months on the road with Q and Not U
years.p: Dischord labelmates [[Q and Not U|a934e33f-b3cb-47dd-9638-f7f1f25fe162]] take Black Eyes across the country. It's the last big push before the band ends.
years.xp: Dischord's bio says the tours with Q and Not U came before the second album, which added saxophone and leaned on improvisation and dub.

years.h: Two months before Cough, Black Eyes play the Black Cat and stop
years.p: The band's final show is at the Black Cat in March 2004. Their second album is due in May.
years.xp: No source I could find says why they quit, so there's no reason given here.

years.h: Cough comes out after the band has split · Dischord No. 145
years.p: Jacob Long has moved to saxophone, and the record leans into improvisation and dub. Wikipedia's summary calls it frenzied brass pushing toward free jazz.

eras.title: Eighteen years in other bands
eras.text: The members spread into electronic music, drone, noise and label work, often alongside each other. No Black Eyes song was played in public again until 2023.

years.p: Jacob Long makes electronic music as [[Earthen Sea|5dbcb05c-6cfd-4fcf-a803-daaac08d328a]], Daniel Martin-McCormick plays in Marriage and [[Mi Ami|0e7ef08c-e735-48f9-a07c-cff6b546c978]], and Hugh McElroy keeps Ruffian going and produces [[Priests|e708ace7-5c5e-48dd-be9b-c5c3aed6273b]].
years.xp: Mike Kanin later started the On Repeat imprint at Astral Spirits.

eras.title: The anniversary that kept going
eras.text: The plan was a few shows of old songs. It turned into new writing, a festival named after the band's own zine, and the first Black Eyes album in twenty-one years, on Dischord again with MacKaye producing.

years.h: The debut gets demos, live sets and a 48-page zine
years.p: Black Eyes returns with unreleased demos and live recordings. Speaking In Tongues: Black Eyes 2001–2004 is a zine history of the band and the DC scene around it.

years.big: "We only played old material and it was really exciting"
years.h: Reunion shows come nineteen years after the last one
years.p: Black Eyes announced the reunion in November 2022 for the debut's 20th anniversary. Martin-McCormick later said they played only old material. Three shows of old songs in April 2023, then new writing by July.
years.xp:
Hugh McElroy told Treble the first plan was only to play the old songs, with no guarantee it would work. Martin-McCormick said rehearsals didn't feel like playing old music.

New ideas were traded remotely, with Kanin sending them from Austin, but didn't come together until all five were in one room in July 2023. Kanin: "it just felt right."

years.cap: Black Eyes at the Black Cat, Washington DC
years.h: Cough turns twenty, with a reissue
years.p: Cough, the album that came out after the breakup, gets a 20th-anniversary reissue while the band keeps touring and trying out new songs.

years.h: Four days of Speaking in Tongues
years.p: Black Eyes name a festival after their 2023 archival zine. It runs October 8 to 11, per Treble.

q: We tracked and mostly mixed it in three days.
years.h: Hostile Design: six new songs, three days, MacKaye again · Dischord No. 199
years.p: Recorded at Tonal Park with [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] producing and Don Godwin engineering. Two drums, bass, guitar and sax as on Cough, now with live multichannel dubbing, drum triggers, samples and some bass clarinet.
years.xp:
The first Black Eyes album in more than two decades was cut fast. Martin-McCormick told Treble they tracked and mostly mixed it in three days.

Treble puts the running time at about 29 minutes, opening with "Break a Leg."
